s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bilateral nasal obstruction, facial pain, and diplopia with abducens nerve palsy
salient_findings: Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Presented with bilateral nasal obstruction
Thick nasal discharge
Facial pain and pressure
Condition recalcitrant to 3 prior surgeries, immunotherapy, and medical therapy
Binocular horizontal diplopia with left lateral gaze
Inability for the left eye to track beyond the midline
Left eye was not proptotic, ecchymotic, or tense
Bedside intraocular pressure measurements: 15 OD, 16 OS (normal)
National Institutes of Health stroke score of 1
Workup results were negative for a cerebrovascular accident
Left-sided abducens nerve palsy resolved by postoperative day 1

differentials: Metastatic disease to the sphenoid sinus
per_call: Metastatic disease to the sphenoid sinus

shortlist.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with painful ophthalmoplegia, including abducens nerve palsy, and can cause facial pain

shortlist.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause abducens nerve palsy and facial pain, and is a medical emergency

shortlist.label: Gradenigo syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Presents with a combination of symptoms including abducens nerve palsy, facial pain, and otitis media

shortlist.label: Sphenoid sinus abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause abducens nerve palsy and facial pain due to its proximity to the cavernous sinus

shortlist.label: Sphenopalatine ganglionitis
shortlist.why_kept: Can cause facial pain and abducens nerve palsy due to its location and potential for inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bilateral nasal obstruction, thick nasal discharge, and facial pain and pressure, along with the development of left-sided abducens nerve palsy that resolved by postoperative day 1, are consistent with sphenopalatine ganglionitis, especially given the recent sphenopalatine ganglion blockade.

rejected.label: Tolosa-Hunt syndrome
rejected.why: Typically presents with painful ophthalmoplegia and is less likely given the resolution of abducens nerve palsy by postoperative day 1

rejected.label: Cavernous sinus thrombosis
rejected.why: Would likely present with more severe symptoms, including proptosis, ecchymosis, and elevated intraocular pressure, which are not present in this case

rejected.label: Gradenigo syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by a specific triad of symptoms (pain in the distribution of the fifth cranial nerve, sixth cranial nerve palsy, and otitis media) not fully matched in this vignette

rejected.label: Sphenoid sinus abscess
rejected.why: Would likely present with more severe symptoms, including fever, headache, and neurological deficits, which are not prominent in this case
